description: This plot illustrates the relationship between "Co-occurrence Number" and "ACC (%)" for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and employs a logarithmic scale with tick labels at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. Data points for all lines are plotted at four distinct x-values, approximately 3, 30, 300, and 3000. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale with major grid lines every 5 units, featuring visible tick labels at 30, 40, 45, 50, and 55 (with a grey rectangle obscuring the area where 35 would be). The "Base" method is represented by a solid black line with circle markers, starting at an ACC of approximately 28 at the first x-value, rising to about 31, and plateauing near 32 for the final two x-values. The "FT" method is shown as a solid blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, beginning at roughly 32, increasing to 36, then to 37, and finishing at approximately 38. The "IKE" method uses a solid red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, starting at about 33, rising to 38, then to 40, and ending at 41. The "MEND" method is depicted by a solid brown line with diamond markers, starting near 36, increasing to 41, reaching 45 at the third point, and remaining steady at 45 at the final point. The "MEMIT" method is represented by a solid purple line with pentagon markers, beginning at approximately 36, rising to 43, then to 46, and concluding at 47. Finally, the "ROME" method is shown as a solid green line with square markers, starting at approximately 44, increasing to 49, rising to 56, and ending at a peak of roughly 59.
